mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to non-triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces revenue growth for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weakening inflationary pressure, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% for two consecutive months signals a sharp contraction in the residential construction sector, which negatively impacts materials and financial firms and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to non-triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month and a fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, ultimately producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher corporate pricing power.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +0.5% AND UNRATE < 4.0% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered periods compared to non-triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 2% for three consecutive months indicates households are accumulating cash rather than spending, which reduces near-term consumption demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.
